inputs.root_cause: Event 231's exact_next_action named UBL-WRITE-001's companion 'write elements in schema-valid order independent of mutation order' obligation as a natural follow-on to the detection-only element-order validation work. While investigating the writer's dumps() function to assess feasibility of auto-reordering, discovered dumps() already calls validate() and raises on any invalid report -- meaning the element-order validation cluster (built in an earlier tick this same session) already, as a side effect, makes dumps() refuse to write out-of-order documents for the checked components. Also discovered dumps() already normalizes any source namespace prefix alias to canonical cbc:/cac:/ext: via ET.register_namespace(), a previously-untested existing behavior.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 4 new tests prove: non-standard source prefixes are normalized to canonical cbc:/cac: on write; dumps() refuses to write a document with checked components out of schema order; dumps() succeeds normally when order is correct.
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite (tests/python/ubl) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read the obligation's full rule_text: 'Write elements in schema-valid order independent of mutation order; offer canonical prefix/formatting policies and lossless mode preserving significant lexical values' -- a compound obligation with 3 distinct clauses.

2. Read writer.py's dumps() function directly before writing any code and found it already calls validate(document, profile=selected_profile, limits=limits) and raises UblWriteError if the report is invalid -- confirming, via direct code inspection, that the element-order validation cluster (an earlier tick this same session, event 231) already wired order-enforcement into the writer as an unplanned but genuine side effect.

3. Probed this directly: constructed a Party with Contact before PostalAddress (wrong schema order) and called dumps() -- confirmed it raises UblWriteError naming the exact violation ('PostalAddress appears after Contact...'), proving the refusal is real and already working, not something that needed new code.

4. Also inspected dumps()'s namespace-prefix handling and found ET.register_namespace() calls registering fixed cbc:/cac:/ext: prefixes -- probed directly with a document declaring a non-standard prefix alias (ns1: instead of cbc:) and confirmed the OUTPUT uses cbc: regardless, proving prefix normalization is also already real, previously-untested behavior.

5. Considered whether to attempt the genuinely unbuilt clause -- automatic silent reordering 'independent of mutation order' -- and deliberately declined: this package's UblDocument/XmlNode model is a raw, ordered-tuple-of-children representation with no higher-level typed builder API (construction is via XmlNode(children=(...)) tuples, not settable named fields), so true mutation-order-independent writing would require either a canonicalization pass or a new architecture-level typed builder API -- a substantial, higher-risk design decision deliberately deferred rather than rushed into this tick.

6. Wrote 4 formal tests proving the two genuinely-already-true findings plus a positive control (correct order succeeds normally), all passing on the first attempt -- zero source code changes were needed for any of them, since both behaviors were already shipped.

7. Ran ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (941 passed, was 937, +4), and the full 6-format regression (3371 passed, was 3367, +4; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
8. No skills-first governance invocation needed -- zero src/ files changed, only new tests and evidence, matching the 'skipped when only tests/evidence YAML change' rule.

9. Promoted the obligation to partial (not implemented): the 'independent of mutation order' clause remains honestly unbuilt, and refusal is a real but distinct guarantee from 'always produces valid output regardless of input order' -- documented transparently in missing_behavior rather than silently claimed as satisfied.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3371 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3367 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule; every claim verified by direct code inspection and interactive probing of already-shipped behavior.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: SAL-UBL-OBL-4BD9BBC9F974C175 (UBL-WRITE-001) missing->partial. Two of the obligation's three clauses proven true (canonical prefix normalization, order-refusal via validate() integration); the third (lossless mode) already covered by pre-existing evidence; the 'independent of mutation order' framing honestly remains unbuilt, distinct from refusal-based enforcement.
